title: Put each empty tote on the tote behind it so it stacks on the full one and nests in the empty one
instruction: Put each empty grey tote on the blue tote behind it so it stacks on the full one and nests in the empty one.
context: Stack-nest totes nest inside each other one way round, to save space when empty, and stack on lugs when turned end for end, so a full tote's contents are not crushed. Hand laborers, material movers and stock clerks handle them all day. Unlike TK-CHXEKF (denesting trays), the robot must read each tote's lugs and recesses against the tote below and whether that tote is full, and leave every tote so nothing inside is crushed.
setup: World frame: x is forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. All four totes are one model of polypropylene stack-nest tote, open-topped, 75 mm tall, with 4 mm walls and floor. The walls lean out 6 degrees, from 134 x 184 mm outside at the base to 150 x 200 mm; the top 20 mm of every wall is a vertical rim lip 12 mm thick, 8 mm of it outside the wall, so the rim is 166 x 216 mm. Each long side wall carries, on the lip's inner face, two yellow lugs 14 mm wide and 10 mm tall, tops 65 mm above the tote's base, standing 10.5 mm out from the lip; they are centred 60 mm toward one end and 25 mm toward the other from the wall's middle. At the same two places the wall's lower 33 mm is a recess 30 mm wide and 12 mm deep, open to the outside and the bottom (seen inside as a dark bump). Two blue totes (fixed) stand with their long sides along y, centred 380 mm in front of the arm bases at 150 mm left and 200 mm right of the midline, lugs 60 mm toward the robot's left of each wall's middle. In lot A (the screenshot) the left blue tote holds a brown cardboard carton of parts, 90 x 150 x 50 mm, 0.4 kg, loose and centred on its floor (top 54.5 mm above the table), and the right one is empty. Two grey totes (loose, 0.15 kg each) stand open side up on the table, turned the same way as the blue totes, centred 180 mm in front of the arm bases at 150 mm left and 200 mm right of the midline, each in front of its blue tote. Nothing else is on the table. Lot B is the same except that the carton is in the right blue tote and the left one is empty. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: The full blue tote and the empty blue tote are scored on their own and earn 0.5 each, so 1.0 when both qualify. The full tote qualifies when a grey tote (either one) stands upright on its yellow lugs, let go and still, with all four outer rim corners 138.5 to 141.5 mm above the table and its centre within 5 mm of the full tote's centre; and at no time in the trial, checked at every control step, did the carton move more than 5 mm or a grey tote's underside (its middle) go below 63 mm above the table over the full tote. The empty tote qualifies when a grey tote is nested in it, upright, let go and still, with all four rim corners 109.27 to 121.27 mm above the table (fully nested is 113.27; a tote can wedge a few mm high in the taper) and its centre within 5 mm of the empty tote's centre. Let go: every finger and gripper of both arms more than 5 mm from that grey tote; while that is unknown, nothing is earned. Still: moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s. Upright: tilted no more than 3 degrees. A tote earns 0 if its grey tote is nested onto the carton (rim about 129.5.5 mm), stacked on the empty tote's lugs, tilted, upside down, held, or elsewhere; the full tote also earns 0 if the carton was moved or a grey tote lowered past its lugs, even if undone later. The trial ends at 1.0 once both qualify for 3 s; otherwise it scores the state at the last step. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Lift both grey totes out of the blue totes. 2. Put the carton on the floor of the blue tote that is full in this trial's lot (lot A: the left one; lot B: the right one), centred. 3. Check that the other blue tote is empty. 4. Set the left grey tote open side up on the table, centred 180 mm in front of the arm bases and 150 mm left of the midline, long sides along y, turned the same way as the blue totes (lugs 60 mm toward the robot's left of each wall's middle). 5. Set the right grey tote the same way, 200 mm right of the midline. 6. Check that nothing else is on the table. Nothing is consumed. Trial k uses lot A when k is even and lot B when k is odd.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX. The totes are 200 x 150 x 75 mm, about two-thirds the footprint of the smallest common stack-nest totes (300 x 200 mm), because the arms cannot carry a full-size tote over another; the taper, offset lugs and recesses and end-for-end rule are kept. Each is 43 boxes; lugs and recesses, not a script, decide stack or nest. Ribs, handholds and rounded corners are left out. Masses are typical; friction is the simulator's default.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B; no grey tote reached a blue tote); demo: 1.0 in each lot (one grey tote turned and stacked on the full tote, the other nested in the empty one)
